newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Black S.African consortium, Ladbroke in casino bid.
newsitem.headline: Black S.African consortium, Ladbroke in casino bid.

text.p: South African black empowerment consortium Mavelani Developments said on Thursday it was bidding for a licence to build an entertainment and gaming resort on the shores of the Vaal Dam near Johannesburg.

Mavelani said in a statement its equity partner in the project was the Ladbroke Group Plc. The Mavelani consortium's share in the project will be 53 percent, of which 10 percent will go to a community development trust.
The consortium said an agreement had been reached that the black empowerment stake would eventually increase to above 70 percent.

The Viking Bay Casino and Hotel resort, planned for a 1,650 hectare site, is expected to include a luxury hotel, entertainment centre, casino, 18-hole golf course bordered by 700 residential units, a predator park and game reserve.
Mavelani chairman Moss Lebakeng Leoka, also president of the Johannesburg Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said the project was driven by the necessity for black empowerment.

"Too often, opportunties such as this one are allocated to the same consortiums or individuals. Our intention here is to ensure that the wealth created is spread over a broader base of black business," he said.
Leoka said the development was expected to create 8,000 jobs. He gave no estimated costs, however.
The gambling and betting board of South Africa's Gauteng province announced earlier this month that it had received 23 applications for its six casino licences.

Legislation passed last year legalised casino gaming in South Africa for the first time and gave control of the running of the industry to the country's nine provinces. Gauteng, the most populous province, is allowed to award the greatest number of licences.

Also on the list are black empowerment group MoAfrika Casino Holdings, which hopes to build a 2.5 billion rand retail and leisure centre, and Tsogo Sun Holdings, a venture between a black consortium and hotel group Southern Sun, which has already secured two licences in Mpumalanga province.
